title: BUG: duplicate top-level 'const MIRRORS' kills Safari background page (extension fully dead)
description:
User-verified in Safari Web Inspector (Develop -> Web Extension Background Content): 'SyntaxError: Can't create duplicate variable: MIRRORS'. Safari MV3 uses background.scripts [archive-url.js, background.js] sharing ONE global lexical scope; archive-url.js declares const MIRRORS and background.js declares const MIRRORS = ArchiveUrl.MIRRORS -> duplicate const -> second script fails to parse -> background never loads -> toolbar, engine, context menu, message handling ALL dead. Root process failure: scripts/test-background.js hit this exact collision in its shared vm context and MASKED it by wrapping each file in an IIFE (documented in its own comment) instead of surfacing it as a production bug.

Fix requirements:
1. extension/background.js: remove the top-level const MIRRORS alias; reference ArchiveUrl.MIRRORS directly at its use sites (pickMirror etc.). Audit background.js for ANY other top-level const/let/function name that also exists top-level in archive-url.js.
2. extension/archive-url.js: wrap the whole file in an IIFE exposing only globalThis.ArchiveUrl, so its internals (MIRRORS, MIRROR_HOSTS, function names) can never collide with a sibling script in any shared scope (background page, content script world, settings page).
3. scripts/test-background.js: REMOVE the IIFE wrapping of loaded files — load archive-url.js and background.js RAW into one shared vm context, exactly as Safari's background page does. Add an explicit test asserting the pair loads without throwing. Same check for the settings harness pattern if it wraps (scripts/test-settings.js loads archive-url.js + settings.js) and the snapshot-probe harness (archive-url.js + snapshot-probe.js).
4. All four suites green after unwrapping; ./build.sh + ./install.sh; user verifies in Safari.

Done: Safari background loads (Develop menu inspector opens without SyntaxError), toolbar archiving works again, and the harness now fails if any future script pair redeclares a shared-scope name.

title: Toggle-click de-archive + configurable auto-redirect lists
description:
Why: the user browses from a news aggregator that inconsistently routes links through archive.ph — often archiving sites they PAY for (where they want the real site, with their login) and not archiving sites they don't. Two features fix this: (1) the toolbar click becomes a TOGGLE — on an archive.ph/mirror page it extracts the original URL and navigates there; on a normal page it archives as today; clicks flip back and forth. (2) Two configurable domain lists drive automatic redirects: 'always-archive' domains are auto-sent to archive.ph, 'always-original' domains are auto-de-archived to the real site. The toggle is the escape hatch that makes automation acceptable: a manual click always wins over the lists.

High-level design (against current extension/background.js + extension/settings/):
- New extension/archive-url.js: pure URL logic (isArchiveUrl across all MIRRORS domains, extractOriginalUrl from newest/<url>, <timestamp>/<url>, <code>/<url>, /o/<code>/<url> forms — null for bare snapshot codes with no embedded URL, buildArchiveUrl, domain normalization + list matching). Node-testable with a fixture table.
- background.js action.onClicked branches on isArchiveUrl(tab.url): de-archive or archive, honoring the existing newTab setting; every manual click records a per-tab manual-override (tabId -> domain) so the auto-redirect engine skips that tab+domain until the tab leaves the domain or closes.
- Settings page grows two list editors backed by storage.local keys alwaysArchiveDomains / alwaysOriginalDomains (normalized lowercase hosts). MUTUAL EXCLUSIVITY enforced on add (adding to one removes from the other, with visible notice) — this plus manual overrides is the loop-prevention story.
- Auto-redirect engine: tabs.onUpdated (changeInfo.url, http/https only; no new permissions needed) applies the lists via tabs.update in the same tab; skips engine-initiated navigations, manual-override tab+domains, and extension pages.

Known limitation (accepted): bare archive.ph short-code URLs (no embedded original URL) cannot be de-archived from the URL alone; the toggle no-ops there. Most snapshot pages canonicalize to <code>/<original-url> where extraction works.
close_reason: All six child beads closed reviewer-passed. Toggle + configurable auto-redirect lists + short-code content-script resolution shipped on epic/6kl.

title: One-command install: curl|bash bootstrap that goes from 0 to installed extension
description:
Why: today a user must clone the repo, know about install.sh, and have prerequisites set up. Goal is a single copy-pasteable command (Homebrew-style) that takes a fresh Mac from 0 to a WORKING extension — which means development-signed where possible, since ad-hoc builds require re-enabling Safari's Allow Unsigned Extensions after every Safari restart (effectively unusable for normal users).

High-level design: add scripts/bootstrap.sh, fetched and run via:
  /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ebowman/archive-ph-safari-plugin/main/scripts/bootstrap.sh)"
The script (1) verifies prerequisites: macOS, git, full Xcode (xcode-select -p pointing at an Xcode.app, xcodebuild usable, license accepted) — with actionable error messages for each failure; (2) auto-detects an Apple Development codesigning identity via the Keychain (security find-identity) and derives the team ID from the certificate subject OU, env-prefixing SIGN_IDENTITY/SIGN_TEAM onto the install.sh invocation only (build.sh already consumes them); if none found, prints a prominent warning (ad-hoc consequence: re-toggle Allow Unsigned Extensions every Safari restart; free fix: Xcode -> Settings -> Accounts -> add Apple ID -> Manage Certificates -> Apple Development) and requires explicit press-Enter confirmation read from /dev/tty before proceeding ad-hoc — aborting nonzero if no tty is available; (3) shallow-clones the repo over HTTPS into a mktemp -d workspace; (4) runs ./install.sh from that clone; (5) removes the temp workspace via an EXIT trap, on success and failure alike.

Design rationale (researched 2026-08-09): temp workspace per rustup precedent (clone is build scratch, not the product; Homebrew/nvm keep clones only because the clone IS the product). Updates = re-run the one-liner. Signing: development signing needs NO paid account — a free Apple ID personal team issues Apple Development certs, and Safari permanently accepts development-signed extensions on the owner's Mac; auto-detection makes the one-liner produce a genuinely usable install with zero configuration, and the unsigned fallback is opt-in via prompt (Homebrew-style) rather than silent. An explicit SIGN_TEAM/SIGN_IDENTITY already in the environment wins over auto-detection and skips the prompt. Manual clone + .signing.env path remains for development.

Note: the raw.githubusercontent URL only works once this lands on main in the public repo.
close_reason: All three child beads closed reviewer-passed: bootstrap.sh implemented (adfdcde), README updated (4ba6534), e2e verification 7/7. One-liner produces a dev-signed working install with zero config on identity-holding machines.

title: Feature additions inspired by octalwise/acidity
description: Gap analysis vs github.com/octalwise/acidity (MIT, same purpose). title: Tighten install flow: make build/install easy and foolproof
description:
Post-debug hardening. Field experience showed three traps: (1) Safari only lists extensions that are development-signed, notarized Developer ID, or App Store — an unnotarized Developer ID build silently counts as UNSIGNED (spctl: 'rejected, source=Unnotarized Developer ID'), and the README currently claims otherwise; (2) having the app both in app/build/ and /Applications makes Safari list the extension twice — the fix is a single installed copy in /Applications with the build copy removed and lsregister-unregistered; (3) build.sh echoes 'Developer ID' for any identity when SIGN_TEAM is set.

Design: an install.sh that makes the happy path one command (build → ditto to /Applications → remove+unregister build copy → open app → tell user the Safari steps), build.sh echo fix, README rewritten around install.sh with an accurate signing matrix (ad-hoc → needs Allow Unsigned Extensions each restart; Apple Development → trusted on your own Mac, recommended for personal use; Developer ID → only with notarization) plus a Troubleshooting section (not listed / listed twice).

Out of scope by choice: automated notarization (needs operator credentials in notarytool; file separately if ever wanted).
close_reason: All 4 beads (3 planned + 1 discovered) implemented, reviewer-passed, committed on epic/xn1. Final install.sh run green: single /Applications copy, single registration.

title: Safari extension: open current page via archive.ph
description:
Personal-use Safari Web Extension: clicking the toolbar icon opens the active tab's URL through archive.ph (https://archive.ph/newest/<url>), which redirects to the newest snapshot or offers to archive if none exists.

High-level design:
- Standard WebExtension (manifest v3): manifest.json + background service worker with an action.onClicked handler that reads the active tab URL and opens the archive.ph URL in a new tab. No content scripts, no permissions beyond 'tabs'.
- Packaged for Safari via 'xcrun safari-web-extension-converter' into a thin macOS wrapper app; run unsigned with Safari's 'Allow Unsigned Extensions' developer option.
- Only http/https URLs are archivable; other schemes (file:, about:, safari-resource:) are ignored.

title: Content script: resolve original URL on bare short-code snapshot pages (aggregator links)
description:
Why (user-reported, 2026-08-10): news aggregators link snapshots as BARE short codes (e.g. https://archive.is/f0rxt). The tab URL never canonicalizes to the <code>/<original-url> long form (verified by user screenshot: tab stays archive.is/f0rxt while the page header shows 'Saved from https://www.ft.com/content/...?syn-...' and 'Redirected from https://www.ft.com/content/...'). extractOriginalUrl therefore returns null, so BOTH the toolbar toggle (6kl.2) and the auto-redirect engine (6kl.4) no-op on exactly the user's primary use case. The 'accepted limitation' is not acceptable for aggregator browsing.

Design:
1. New extension/snapshot-probe.js content script, registered in manifest.json content_scripts with matches for all seven MIRRORS hosts (https://archive.ph/*, archive.today, archive.fo, archive.is, archive.li, archive.md, archive.vn), run_at document_end. NOTE: Safari will ask the user to grant per-site permission for these domains the first time — document this consequence in the bead notes at implementation time; it is expected UX, not a bug.
2. The script runs ONLY when the page URL has no embedded original (delegate the check to a tiny inline equivalent or just always report). Extraction order, tolerant to layout drift: (a) the 'Redirected from' input value (clean URL, no tracking params) if present; (b) the 'Saved from' input value; (c) any <a> in the header area whose href is an absolute http(s) URL to a non-mirror host; (d) og:url / rel=canonical if they carry a non-mirror URL. Validate: http(s) only, host not a MIRRORS host, else report nothing.
3. On success, api.runtime.sendMessage({type:'snapshot-original', originalUrl}) — background stores tabId -> originalUrl in a module map (cleared on tabs.onRemoved with the existing cleanup, and overwritten on each new report for that tab).
4. background.js consumers: (a) toggle — when extractOriginalUrl(tab.url) is null, fall back to the stored originalUrl for that tab before giving up; (b) engine — on receiving snapshot-original, run the SAME de-archive rule (original's domain on alwaysOriginalDomains, corrupted-storage guard, manual-override check, engine marker set before update) and tabs.update to the original. The message path replaces onUpdated for this case since the URL never changes.
5. pbxproj: wire snapshot-probe.js into the appex Resources phase EXACTLY like archive-url.js (relative path, additive entries only — see 6kl.3 commit c048374 for the pattern).
6. Tests: extend the node harnesses — fixture HTML strings modeled on the real page (header inputs with saved-from/redirected-from values, incl. a ?syn- tracking-param variant where redirected-from must win) driving the extraction function (make it pure and attach to a global like the other logic); background message-path cases: bare-code tab + report + domain on alwaysOriginalDomains -> tabs.update to original; manual-override suppresses it; unlisted domain -> no call; mirror-host original rejected; toggle fallback uses stored URL. Mutation-verify at least the redirected-from-preference and the override guard.

Done-criteria: all node suites green including new cases; node --check on all changed JS; python3 -m json.tool manifest clean; ./build.sh succeeds and built appex Resources contains snapshot-probe.js; live verification on https://archive.is/f0rxt with ft.com on the always-original list is HUMAN smoke at merge (record as residual).

Limitation that remains: pages where archive.today serves an interstitial/CAPTCHA before content; extraction simply reports nothing and behavior degrades to today's no-op.

title: Settings: always-archive / always-original domain list editors with mutual exclusivity
description:
Input: extension/settings/{settings.html,settings.css,settings.js} (currently a single newTab preference), ArchiveUrl.normalizeDomain from 6kl.1 (load archive-url.js into settings.html via a script tag before settings.js).

Deliverable: settings page changes only (plus the script tag). Storage schema (storage.local, same area as newTab): alwaysArchiveDomains: string[] and alwaysOriginalDomains: string[] — normalized lowercase hosts, no scheme/path, deduped, stable order (append; no sorting).

UI, matching the existing page's structure and styling:
1. Two sections with user-facing labels that explain semantics, NOT allow/block jargon: 'Always open via archive.ph' (sites you don't pay for) and 'Always open the original site' (sites you pay for — links to archive.ph copies of these get un-archived automatically). One text input + Add button + removable list per section (button or x per entry).
2. Input handling: run entries through ArchiveUrl.normalizeDomain; reject invalid input with an inline message, never silently. Pasting a full URL must work (normalization strips scheme/path).
3. MUTUAL EXCLUSIVITY (loop prevention, load-bearing): adding a domain to one list removes it from the other, with a visible inline notice ('moved from the other list'). Enforce on every add; also self-heal on load — if storage somehow contains a domain in both lists, drop it from alwaysArchiveDomains and keep alwaysOriginalDomains (prefer the user reaching their paid site), one-line comment explaining the tiebreak.
4. Persistence: read on load, write on every mutation; page reflects storage after reload.
5. Non-goals: no background.js changes; the lists have no effect yet (engine lands in 6kl.4) — fine for this bead.

Done-criteria: node --check extension/settings/settings.js clean; settings.html still valid (opens, no console errors); manual verification on built extension (./install.sh sanctioned): add domains incl. a pasted full URL to both lists, remove entries, restart the settings page and see persistence, add the same domain to both lists sequentially and observe the move + notice; storage inspected (or a temporary debug readout) shows normalized deduped arrays.

title: Toolbar click toggles: de-archive on archive pages, archive elsewhere, with per-tab manual override
description:
Input: extension/background.js after 6kl.1 (ArchiveUrl helpers available), existing action.onClicked handler (currently always archives) and newTab setting logic (shouldUseNewTab).

Deliverable: background.js changes only.
1. action.onClicked: if ArchiveUrl.isArchiveUrl(tab.url): extract original via ArchiveUrl.extractOriginalUrl; if non-null, navigate to it honoring the existing newTab setting (tabs.update same tab when newTab=false, tabs.create otherwise — mirror the openArchive tab logic); if null (bare short-code), do nothing (accepted limitation, add a one-line comment). Else (non-archive page): existing openArchive path unchanged.
2. Manual override registry, consumed later by the auto-redirect engine (bead 6kl.4): module-level Map tabId -> Set of normalized domains the user manually toggled in that tab. On EVERY manual toolbar/context-menu action (both directions — archiving AND de-archiving), record the ORIGINAL article's domain (for de-archive: domain of the extracted original URL; for archive: domain of the page being archived) into the map for the tab that ends up displaying the result (the clicked tab when reusing, the new tab id from tabs.create's resolved tab otherwise). On api.tabs.onRemoved, delete the tab's entry. Expose as small named functions (e.g. recordManualOverride(tabId, url), hasManualOverride(tabId, url), the latter using ArchiveUrl.urlMatchesDomain) so 6kl.4 can call them — but nothing reads them yet in this bead.
3. Context menu behavior unchanged (always archives) except it also records the override per 2.
4. Non-goals: no list logic, no auto-redirect, no settings changes.

Edge cases to handle explicitly: tab.url undefined/non-http (existing guard stays first); extractOriginalUrl returning a URL whose scheme is not http(s) is impossible by 6kl.1's contract (returns null) — still guard openArchive-style before tabs.update; tabs.create promise rejection must not surface (match existing openArchiveSafe pattern).

Done-criteria: node --check extension/background.js clean; node scripts/test-archive-url.js still exits 0; manual smoke on the built extension (./install.sh, sanctioned): (a) click on a normal article page opens its archive as before; (b) click while viewing an archive.ph/<code>/<url> page navigates to the original URL; (c) clicking again re-archives — toggle demonstrated both directions with newTab=false for a clean same-tab loop; (d) click on a bare archive.ph short-code page (mid-redirect) does nothing and throws nothing (check via Safari Web Inspector background console if reachable, else absence of visible breakage).

title: archive-url.js: pure URL helpers + node fixture tests
description:
Input: extension/background.js (MIRRORS list lines 5-13, #-encoding logic line 75, mirror URL construction line 77), extension/manifest.json (background.scripts array + service_worker).

Deliverable: new extension/archive-url.js exposing pure functions on a single global (e.g. globalThis.ArchiveUrl = {...}), plus scripts/test-archive-url.js (node, zero deps) with a fixture table.

Functions:
1. isArchiveUrl(url) -> bool: true iff the URL's host is one of the MIRRORS hosts (archive.ph/today/fo/is/li/md/vn — move the MIRRORS array into this file and have background.js consume ArchiveUrl.MIRRORS so the list lives in one place).
2. extractOriginalUrl(url) -> string|null: for archive URL paths of the forms newest/<url>, wip/<url>, <14-digit-timestamp>/<url>, <code>/<url>, o/<code>/<url> — find the first embedded http:// or https:// occurrence in the path and return everything from there, decoding %23 back to # (inverse of the existing safeUrl encoding). Return null for: non-archive hosts, bare short-code paths with no embedded URL, non-http(s) embedded schemes.
3. buildArchiveUrl(mirrorBase, url) -> string: extract the existing '#'->%23 + ${base}/newest/${safeUrl} logic from background.js openArchive.
4. normalizeDomain(input) -> string|null: for settings entry — trim, lowercase, strip scheme, path, port, trailing dots, leading 'www.'; return null for empty/invalid results.
5. urlMatchesDomain(url, domain) -> bool: host === domain or host ends with '.'+domain.

Wiring: manifest.json background.scripts becomes ["archive-url.js", "background.js"] (Safari path); background.js top gains a guarded importScripts for the Chrome service_worker path: if (typeof importScripts === 'function' && typeof ArchiveUrl === 'undefined') importScripts('archive-url.js'). background.js MIRRORS const replaced by ArchiveUrl.MIRRORS and openArchive uses ArchiveUrl.buildArchiveUrl. NO behavior change in this bead — click still always archives.

Test: scripts/test-archive-url.js loads extension/archive-url.js (fs.readFileSync + eval or vm.runInThisContext), runs a fixture table covering: every mirror domain recognized; newest/, wip/, timestamp, code/<url>, o/code/<url> extraction; %23 round-trip (archive of https://a.com/x#frag extracts back with #frag); bare code -> null; javascript: embedded scheme -> null; normalizeDomain cases (scheme+path stripped, www. stripped, uppercase lowered, garbage -> null); urlMatchesDomain exact + subdomain + no-false-positive (notexample.com vs example.com). Exits nonzero on any failure, prints per-case pass/fail.

Done-criteria: node scripts/test-archive-url.js exits 0 with all cases passing; node --check on both extension/background.js and extension/archive-url.js; python3 -m json.tool extension/manifest.json clean; behavior unchanged (click archives as before) — verify by reading the diff, no e2e needed here.

title: Auto-redirect engine: apply domain lists on navigation, never fighting manual toggles
description:
Input: background.js after 6kl.2 (ArchiveUrl helpers, manual-override registry recordManualOverride/hasManualOverride), storage schema from 6kl.3 (alwaysArchiveDomains/alwaysOriginalDomains). No new manifest permissions: use api.tabs.onUpdated (tabs permission already present).

1. Listener on api.tabs.onUpdated firing only when changeInfo.url is set. Guard order (each with early return): non-http(s) URL; hasManualOverride(tabId, relevantUrl) — for archive URLs the relevant URL is the extracted original, for normal URLs the URL itself; engine-initiated marker (see 3).
2. Rules, evaluated against fresh storage.local reads (cheap; no caching layer in this bead):
   a. De-archive rule: isArchiveUrl(url) and extractOriginalUrl(url) non-null and original's domain matches alwaysOriginalDomains -> tabs.update(tabId, original). Always same tab: this is a redirect correction, not a user action, so the newTab setting does NOT apply (state this in a comment).
   b. Archive rule: NOT isArchiveUrl(url) and url's domain matches alwaysArchiveDomains -> tabs.update(tabId, ArchiveUrl.buildArchiveUrl(mirror, url)). Use MIRRORS[0] (archive.ph) directly — do NOT call pickMirror here, its sequential HEAD probes are too slow/chatty to run on every navigation (comment this; the manual click path keeps pickMirror).
3. Engine-initiated marker: before each tabs.update, record tabId -> target URL in a module map; in the listener, if changeInfo.url equals the recorded target (or a prefix match after archive.ph's own redirects — exact match is acceptable, note the tradeoff), consume the marker and return. Entries also cleared on tabs.onRemoved (share the cleanup with the manual-override map).
4. Loop analysis to encode in comments: mutual exclusivity of lists (6kl.3) prevents A->B->A cross-rule loops; the archive rule's output is an archive URL (host not on alwaysArchiveDomains since those are article domains) so it cannot re-trigger rule b; rule a's output could re-trigger rule b ONLY if the same domain were on both lists — excluded by 6kl.3, and the engine-initiated marker is the belt-and-braces backstop. Rule a must also NOT fire when the extracted original's domain matches alwaysArchiveDomains (defensive check against corrupted storage).
5. Storage read failures: treat as empty lists (never throw, never block navigation).
